AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: The aims of the current study were to (1) determine the association between personal income and body mass index (BMI) and between individual education and BMI, and (2) examine the association between education and BMI across strata of personal income among women.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: The design of the study was a quantitative analysis of data from self-report questionnaires.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: The study setting was socioeconomically disadvantaged neighborhoods in Victoria, Australia.

AbstractText.Label: SUBJECTS
AbstractText.content: The study included 4065 nonpregnant women (ages 18-45 years) living in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas.

AbstractText.Label: MEASURES
AbstractText.content: The study used a self-report questionnaire measuring sociodemographic characteristics known to be associated with BMI.

AbstractText.Label: ANALYSIS
AbstractText.content: Multiple linear regressions with imputation were used to assess the association between education level, personal income, and BMI, while controlling for covariates.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Mean (SD) observed BMI was 26.0 (6.1) kg/m2. Compared with women with low education, women with medium (b = -0.81; 95% confidence interval, -1.30 to -0.27; p = .004) and high (b = -1.71; 95% confidence interval, -2.34 to -1.09; p < .001) education had statistically significantly lower BMI values. No differences in BMI were observed between income categories. Stratified analyses suggested that the education-BMI association may be stronger in low-income than higher-income women.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Our data show that among women living in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas, high education level rather than personal income may be protective against overweight/obesity. High personal income, however, may buffer the effects of low education on BMI. Obesity prevention efforts should target women with amplified disadvantage.
